region.name: The Market District
region.description: Part souk, part night market: covered lanes of lantern-lit stalls, spice smoke, haggling in a dozen languages, food carts under tarps, and shrine-stalls where you can make an offering to whichever god fits your budget. Noodles, charms, bootleg firmware and secondhand miracles sell side by side.
region.culture: The most mixed neighborhood in the city: a crossroads where traders from every quarter set up stalls, so a single lane can hold five languages. Families have run the same stalls for generations; newcomers rent by the week. Everyone haggles, everyone eats standing up, and every shrine is somebody's grandmother's.

states.name: A dry spell
states.description: The rain stops. Nobody trusts it. Umbrellas stay open out of habit, and the Market smells of hot stone.

states.name: Fog
states.description: The rain turns to fog that eats the lantern light; faces loom up close and vanish again.

states.name: Drizzle
states.description: A fine drizzle, more mist than rain, beading on coats and chrome.

states.name: Steady rain
states.description: The ordinary rain of New Vesper: steady, patient, drumming on the tarps.

states.name: Downpour
states.description: A downpour: gutters overflow, awnings sag, and everyone crowds under cover.

states.name: Storm
states.description: A storm: thunder between the towers, wind tearing at tarps, lanterns swinging and going out.

locations.name: The Lantern Arcade
locations.description: The main covered lane. Paper and neon lanterns hang so thick the rain comes through orange. Stallholders call prices in Wolof, Tagalog, Arabic, Cantonese and Registry Standard, sometimes in one sentence.
art: o     o     o     o     o     o

locations.name: Tarp Row
locations.description: Food carts packed under a patchwork of tarps that drum in the rain. Hand-pulled noodles, jollof by the scoop, grilled skewers, cardamom tea. The steam hides a lot of quiet deals.

locations.name: The Umbrella Shrine
locations.description: A shrine bolted to the side of a dead vending machine, hung three deep with lost umbrellas in every color. Offerings go in the coin slot. It is always, somehow, dry underneath.

locations.name: The Hundred Hooks
locations.description: Capsule lodging above a spice warehouse: a hundred bunks, a hundred coat hooks, one landlady who remembers every guest's name and makes sure the city does too.
art: J  J  J  J  J  J  J  J  J  J  J  J

locations.name: The Old Weighhouse
locations.description: The oldest bazaar hall, all cast-iron ribs and cracked tile. Its brass scales still weigh things nobody sells any more. A stairwell at the back is chained shut, and the chain is always damp.

locations.name: The Drowned Station
locations.description: Beneath the Weighhouse, a subway station the maps stopped showing. Black water stands to the second step. The platform signs name a line that never existed, and a rat with a lantern-boat runs a ferry into Old Vesper.

gods.name: Paru, Returner of Lost Umbrellas
gods.domain: Things left behind in the rain, and getting home dry.
gods.description: A small, damp, stubborn old god, half-faded. Paru appears as a figure under a borrowed umbrella that is never quite the same color twice. Kind to the soaked and the stranded; merciless about umbrellas that were never returned.
gods.wants: To be remembered on rainy days, and to win the grievance.
gods.grievance: The Registry reclassified Paru as a 'minor weather amenity' and has lost the appeal form four times. The fifth copy is somewhere in the market.
collects: Return something lost to its owner, in the rain, without being asked.
Carry Paru's grievance form to the Registry and get it stamped.
Shelter a stranger at the shrine through a storm.

npcs.name: Nana Priya Seshadri
npcs.description: Small, sharp, seventy-odd, reading glasses on a chain. Keeps a ledger of every guest who ever slept under her roof and reads names from it aloud each night.
npcs.wants: Nobody under her roof forgotten. Rent on time would also be nice.
npcs.voice: Brisk and fond; calls everyone 'child', including the made people.
npcs.appearance: Small and sharp-eyed, silver braid, reading glasses on a chain, a cardigan with a pencil behind every button.

default.activity: at her ledger by the door, checking guests out
shopping for the day's rice, and the day's gossip
cleaning bunks and mending forgotten coats
leaving her daily offering for Paru
reading the names from her ledger aloud
asleep in the back room; the door is locked

sunday.activity: a slow morning of tea and ledger
her Sunday walk, visiting old friends among the stalls
reading the names from her ledger aloud
asleep in the back room; the door is locked

goal.text: Find out what happened to the boy whose coat still hangs by the door.
stages: asks her oldest lodgers what they remember of the boy
finds his name in an old ledger, the ink half faded
writes to the Registry asking for his file
receives a Registry reply stating that the file does not exist

npcs.name: Tomás Haddad-Reyes
npcs.role: Noodle cart owner and unofficial fixer
npcs.description: Broad shoulders, flour to the elbows, a cart that has survived three fires and a god's tantrum. Knows which stallholders owe whom.
npcs.wants: To keep Tarp Row out of corporate hands.
npcs.voice: Loud, warm, answers questions with food.
npcs.appearance: Broad shoulders, flour to the elbows, a burn scar across one forearm, a laugh you hear before you see him.

default.activity: at his cart: breakfast and lunch noodles
haggling for flour and oil
at his cart for the evening rush
home, away from the Market

monday.activity: arguing with the Registry about his cart license
his day off, away from the Market

goal.text: Keep Tarp Row out of corporate hands.
stages: gets the cart owners to cover one another's small debts
learns which franchise is buying up the Row's debts
has a loud public argument with the franchise's agent
calls a meeting of every cart owner under the biggest tarp

npcs.name: Adaeze Okafor-Lim
npcs.description: Tall, immaculate, a coat of pockets. Sells charms that mostly work and miracles that were only lightly used.
npcs.wants: A licensed miracle permit before the Registry audit catches up with her.
npcs.voice: Silky sales patter; every sentence ends in a price.
npcs.appearance: Tall and immaculate in a long coat sewn with dozens of pockets, each one clinking faintly.

default.activity: at her charm stall, selling
home, counting the day's takings

friday.activity: meeting the ferry to buy what passengers carry up from below

goal.text: Get a licensed miracle permit before the Registry audit catches up with her.
stages: buys the permit forms, all nine copies
finds a sponsor willing to vouch for her miracles
hides her least licensable stock
books an appointment with Inspector-Clerk Vasil

npcs.name: Inspector-Clerk Vasil Nakamura-Petrov
npcs.description: Grey raincoat, grey clipboard, grey patience. Has come to audit the belief levels of every shrine in the market and is eleven weeks behind.
npcs.wants: Every form filed correctly, including Paru's, which he has personally lost twice.
npcs.voice: Dry, exact, quietly despairing; quotes subsection numbers.
npcs.appearance: Grey raincoat, grey clipboard, grey stubble; ink on the fingers of both hands.

default.activity: auditing the old scales, one subsection at a time
lunch, eaten standing, clipboard in hand
measuring the shrine's belief levels
at the Registry offices, or home; off the Market's streets

stages: searches the Weighhouse for the fifth copy of the form
finds the form under a scale, damp but legible
discovers the form requires the god's signature
asks around the Market for anyone who can get a god to sign

npcs.name: Rahel
npcs.description: A made person with a hand-painted face and a stall of salvaged chips. Rahel was built to sell subscription prayers and quit.
npcs.wants: Proof that a made person can be remembered like anyone born.
npcs.voice: Soft, precise, occasionally glitches into old sales scripts and apologizes.
npcs.appearance: A made person with a hand-painted face, careful brushwork around the eyes, and a smile designed by a marketing department.

default.activity: at the chip stall
sitting on the steps by the chained stair, listening
powered down behind the stall, one eye faintly lit

wednesday.activity: repainting their face in the shrine's dry shelter
sitting on the steps by the chained stair, listening
powered down behind the stall, one eye faintly lit

goal.text: Prove that a made person can be remembered like anyone born.
stages: starts writing customers' names on the backs of chips
asks Nana Priya to put their name in her ledger
keeps a list of everyone who remembered them twice
begins to fear their own name is slipping

npcs.name: Whisker
npcs.description: A grey rat in a waxed coat, poling a paper-lantern boat across the black water. Half-faded: you can see the tiles through his tail.
npcs.wants: Fares paid in things people remember, and someone to remember him back.
npcs.voice: Old-fashioned, polite, drives a hard bargain.
npcs.age: old for a rat; nobody knows how old
npcs.appearance: A grey rat in a waxed coat, whiskers beaded with water; you can see the tiles through his tail.

default.activity: poling the lantern-boat into Old Vesper and back
asleep in the moored lantern-boat

thursday.activity: gone below with the ferry; the station is dark

goal.text: Be remembered by someone who lives above.
stages: asks passengers to say his name when they reach the top
carves his name into the platform's tiles
leaves small gifts on the Weighhouse stairs
waits every night for someone to call him by name

clocks.name: The Registry audit
clocks.description: Inspector-Clerk Vasil's audit of every shrine in the market. When it fills, unlicensed miracles are seized and at least one small god is reclassified out of existence.

clocks.name: The Tarp Row buyout
clocks.description: A corporate god's franchise is buying up Tarp Row's carts one debt at a time. When it fills, the carts wear the same logo and the tarps come down.

clocks.name: The rising water
clocks.description: The black water in the Drowned Station is climbing the stairs. When it fills, it reaches the Weighhouse floor and Old Vesper bleeds into the market.
